finding.claim: deleteAccount ignores the result of canDelete, so any non-admin authenticated user can delete any account by ID (broken authorization).
finding.source: Authenticated non-admin caller User u and attacker-chosen id from DELETE /accounts/{id} (per comment at line 19).

trace.note: canDelete(u, a) called; boolean result discarded

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) implements owner-or-admin correctly but its result is unused; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) which throws on denial is not called in deleteAccount (closeAccount calls it at line 29); no other check in the file. Fix: call assertCanDelete(u, a) at line 22.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a bool that line 22 discards as a bare statement; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) would throw but is not called in deleteAccount (it is only used at line 29 in closeAccount). No other check exists between the call and accounts.remove(id) at line 23.
verdict.reason: deleteAccount at AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete and discards its boolean result, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller, and an authenticated non-admin can delete accounts they do not own. The only caveat is that the file does not show the router, so whether the caller is authenticated is assumed from the comment, not verified here.

finding.claim: Account-existence oracle and unhandled null: for a missing ID, non-admins get NullPointerException while foreign-owned accounts yield SecurityException, letting an attacker enumerate valid account IDs.
finding.source: Attacker-chosen id and any authenticated non-admin caller.
finding.sink: Authorization decision in canDelete (a.ownerId() dereference) reached from deleteAccount (line 22) and closeAccount (line 29).

trace.note: accounts.get(id) returns null for missing id
a.ownerId() dereferences null for non-admin, throwing NPE
for existing foreign account, SecurityException("not allowed") is thrown instead, producing a distinguishable response

finding.guards_checked: Admin short-circuit at line 10 (admins unaffected); no null check before ownership evaluation anywhere in the file.

verdict.guard_found: Admin short-circuit at src/AccountService.java:10 (admins only, not a guard against non-admins). No null check on `a` before `a.ownerId()` at line 10. assertCanDelete (line 13-17) throws SecurityException and is not caught, so it is an effective check only on the closeAccount path (line 29), where it runs after the NPE-prone line 10 call and so does not stop the null case. On deleteAccount (line 22), canDelete's bool result is discarded, so no guard applies there at all.
verdict.reason: For an authenticated non-admin, closeAccount (src/AccountService.java:28-29) yields an NPE from line 10 when the id is missing and a SecurityException from line 15 when the account exists but is foreign, so the two responses distinguish existence; the trace lines match the code. The candidate's sink list is imprecise because deleteAccount (line 22) discards canDelete's result and enforces nothing, which is a separate and more serious authorization bug the finding does not mention.

finding.claim: Unsynchronized shared mutable Map; concurrent closeAccount/deleteAccount calls can race on a non-thread-safe map. Unverified: concrete map type and any synchronization are not visible in this file.
finding.source: Concurrent requests to the mutating methods.

trace.note: plain non-final Map field, no synchronization

finding.guards_checked: None in this file. Synchronization, if any, would be at map construction, which is outside the audited code. Treat as candidate to confirm.

verdict.guard_found: The check-then-act in closeAccount is guarded by assertCanDelete at src/AccountService.java:29, which throws SecurityException before remove at line 30. The race cannot change the outcome because this file never inserts into `accounts`, so the value at `id` cannot be swapped between the check (line 28-29) and the remove (line 30). The map's thread safety depends on its construction, which is not in this file.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file (line 4 plain field, lines 28-30 read/check/remove, line 23 remove), but a race at src/AccountService.java:28-30 cannot change which account is authorized or removed because nothing in this file re-keys the map, so it is not an authorization bypass; the only remaining concern (thread safety of the Map) is not decidable here. Separately, src/AccountService.java:22 discards the canDelete result in deleteAccount, which is a real missing-authorization bug that the candidate did not report.
